claim: Reduced expression of KChIP2 is consistently observed in numerous cardiac pathologies.
source: Amongst a multitude of remodeling events, reduced expression of the ion channel subunit KChIP2 is consistently observed in numerous cardiac pathologies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known observation from prior research.

claim: KChIP2 transcriptionally represses miR-34b and miR-34c.
source: Through interaction with genetic elements, KChIP2 transcriptionally repressed the miRNAs miR-34b and miR-34c, which subsequently targeted key depolarizing (INa) and repolarizing (Ito) currents altered in cardiac disease.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including luciferase assays and ChIP experiments.

claim: miR-34b and miR-34c target depolarizing (INa) and repolarizing (Ito) currents.
source: Through interaction with genetic elements, KChIP2 transcriptionally repressed the miRNAs miR-34b and miR-34c, which subsequently targeted key depolarizing (INa) and repolarizing (Ito) currents altered in cardiac disease.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by patch clamp data and molecular targeting experiments.

claim: Maintaining KChIP2 expression under pathologic conditions restored channel function.
source: Genetically maintaining KChIP2 expression or inhibiting miR-34 under pathologic conditions restored channel function and moreover, prevented the incidence of reentrant arrhythmias.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by phenylephrine treatment experiments with adenoviral KChIP2 delivery.

claim: Inhibiting miR-34 under pathologic conditions prevented the incidence of reentrant arrhythmias.
source: Genetically maintaining KChIP2 expression or inhibiting miR-34 under pathologic conditions restored channel function and moreover, prevented the incidence of reentrant arrhythmias.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by optical mapping experiments showing prevention of sustained reentry.

claim: KChIP2 associates with and modulates the Kv4 family of potassium channels.
source: It is well described that KChIP2 associates with and modulates the Kv4 family of potassium channels, which together define the fast transient outward potassium current (Ito,f), maintaining early cardiac repolarization (An et al., 2000; Niwa and Nerbonne, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: KChIP2 and Kv4 channels together define the fast transient outward potassium current (Ito,f).
source: It is well described that KChIP2 associates with and modulates the Kv4 family of potassium channels, which together define the fast transient outward potassium current (Ito,f), maintaining early cardiac repolarization (An et al., 2000; Niwa and Nerbonne, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: KChIP2 knock-down shows reduced transcript expression for SCN5A and SCN1B.
source: Investigations following KChIP2 knock-down show reduced transcript expression for the cardiac sodium channel gene, SCN5A, and its accessory subunit SCN1B, in addition to Kv4.3 protein, prompting the loss of both Ito,f and INa (Deschênes et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a prior finding with citation and is confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: KChIP2 knock-down results in loss of Kv4.3 protein.
source: Investigations following KChIP2 knock-down show reduced transcript expression for the cardiac sodium channel gene, SCN5A, and its accessory subunit SCN1B, in addition to Kv4.3 protein, prompting the loss of both Ito,f and INa (Deschênes et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a prior finding with citation and is confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: Other members of the KChIP family not expressed in the myocardium behave as transcriptional repressors.
source: Indeed, other members of the KChIP family not expressed in the myocardium behave as transcriptional repressors, while also maintaining the ability to interact with Kv4 channels (An et al., 2000; Carrión et al., 1999; Savignac et al., 2005; Gomez-Villafuertes et al., 2005; Ronkainen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: KChIP2 silencing in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes resulted in the induction of a number of miRNAs.
source: We therefore performed a miRNA microarray following KChIP2 silencing in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs), resulting in the induction of a number of miRNAs (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by microarray data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: miR-34b and miR-34c are predicted to target SCN5A, SCN1B, and KCND3.
source: Ultimately, we identified miR-34b and −34c as the only miRNAs predicted to target not just one of these ion channel genes, but notably target all three collectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from TargetScan analysis and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Real-time qPCR confirmed elevation in the mature transcripts for miR-34b and miR-34c following KChIP2 silencing.
source: Real-time qPCR was used to confirm the array results, showing elevation in the mature transcripts for miR-34b and −34c (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding confirmed by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Overexpression of three different cardiac KChIP2 isoforms reduced the expression of miRs-34b/c.
source: Importantly, we also performed overexpression of three different cardiac KChIP2 isoforms which reduced the expression of miRs-34b/c (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Endogenous KChIP2 localizes to the nucleus in adult rat cardiomyocytes.
source: Indeed, fractionation of adult rat cardiomyocytes into nuclear fractions reveals endogenous KChIP2 nuclear expression in the absence of contaminating cytosolic (lactate dehydrogenase) and membrane associated proteins (Serca2a) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown by fractionation and immunoblotting in Figure 1E.

claim: KChIP2 colocalizes in the nucleus of adult cardiomyocytes.
source: This is reinforced in the localization patterns of adult cardiomyocytes, showing marked endogenous KChIP2 colocalization in the nucleus in the absence of the cytosolic marker lactate dehydrogenase (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 1F.

claim: miR-34b and miR-34c are transcribed in tandem under the regulation of a shared, intergenic promoter.
source: Notably, both miR-34b and −34c are transcribed in tandem under the regulation of a shared, intergenic promoter (Toyota et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: A potential DRE motif site exists 254 bp upstream of the miR-34b stem-loop in the miR-34b/c promoter.
source: MatInspector software (Cartharius et al., 2005) was used to evaluate the miR-34b/c promoter for occurrences of this motif, revealing a potential site beginning 254 bp upstream of the miR-34b stem-loop (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computational analysis using MatInspector software.

claim: KChIP2 isoforms (2.3, 2.4, and 2.6) significantly repress the miR-34b/c promoter in luciferase assays.
source: When compared to a GFP transfected control without KChIP2, we observed significant repression in the presence of KChIP2.3, 2.4, and 2.6 (Figure 2A), showing that KChIP2 can directly act on the miR-34b/c promoter to impart repressive action.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from luciferase assays shown in Figure 2A.

claim: KChIP2 physically interacts with the miR-34b/c promoter at the DRE site.
source: KChIP2 pull-down resulted in significant enrichment of the DRE containing PCR fragment when compared to an IgG control (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from ChIP-PCR shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Transfection of miR-34b/c precursors into NRVMs reduced mRNA for SCN5A and SCN1B.
source: Assessment of the resulting transcripts showed reduced mRNA for SCN5A and SCN1B following miR-34 expression, compared to a non-targeting control miR (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 3A.

claim: KCND3 mRNA levels remained unchanged following miR-34b/c precursor transfection in NRVMs.
source: While KCND3 levels remained unchanged (Figure 3A), Kv4.3 protein experienced significant reduction that reinforces the miRNA mode of translational inhibition without mRNA degradation previously noted (Deschênes et al., 2008) (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Kv4.3 protein experienced significant reduction following miR-34b/c precursor transfection despite unchanged KCND3 mRNA.
source: While KCND3 levels remained unchanged (Figure 3A), Kv4.3 protein experienced significant reduction that reinforces the miRNA mode of translational inhibition without mRNA degradation previously noted (Deschênes et al., 2008) (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from immunoblotting shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: miR-34b/c target the 3'-UTR of SCN5A, SCN1B, and KCND3 genes.
source: This construct was co-expressed with the miR-34b/c precursors in HEK293 cells, resulting in reduced activity in all three constructs when compared to a control miR-precursor (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Mutations in the seed region of the 3'-UTR significantly attenuated the repressive action of miR-34b/c.
source: Subsequently, mutations were made within the seed region where miR-34 targeting is predicted to bind (Figure 3D), which significantly attenuated the repressive action (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from luciferase reporter assays with mutated 3'-UTRs shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Expression of miR-34b/c precursor produced a significant decline in INa in NRVMs.
source: Reflecting the changes in mRNA and protein, expression of miR-34b/c precursor produced a significant decline in INa (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 3F.

claim: miR-34b/c expression resulted in a significant reduction in Ito,f density in NRVMs.
source: We therefore modified our patch protocol to probe just Ito,f and remove the contribution of Kv1.4, which now revealed a significant reduction in the Ito,f density (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Expression of miR-34b/c precursors in human iCells produced a significant loss in Ito density.
source: Expression of miR-34b/c precursors now produced a significant loss in Ito density (Figure 3J), while also maintaining reductions in INa (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings in human iCells shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Phenylephrine stimulation resulted in a dramatic decline of KCNIP2 (KChIP2) in NRVMs.
source: PE stimulation resulted in a dramatic decline of KCNIP2 (KChIP2), while also yielding significant elevation in miR-34b/c (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Phenylephrine stimulation yielded significant elevation in miR-34b/c in NRVMs.
source: PE stimulation resulted in a dramatic decline of KCNIP2 (KChIP2), while also yielding significant elevation in miR-34b/c (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Phenylephrine treatment resulted in reductions in expression for SCN5A, SCN1B, and KCND3 transcripts in NRVMs.
source: These conditions resulted in reductions in expression for SCN5A, SCN1B, and KCND3 transcripts (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Maintaining KChIP2 levels through adenovirus normalized the expression of miRs-34b/c during phenylephrine treatment.
source: Critically, maintaining KChIP2 levels through use of adenovirus encoding KChIP2 (Ad.KChIP2) normalized the expression of miRs-34b/c while reversing the loss in SCN5A and SCN1B; however, KCND3 levels remained suppressed (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Ad.KChIP2 treatment reversed the loss in SCN5A and SCN1B during phenylephrine treatment.
source: Critically, maintaining KChIP2 levels through use of adenovirus encoding KChIP2 (Ad.KChIP2) normalized the expression of miRs-34b/c while reversing the loss in SCN5A and SCN1B; however, KCND3 levels remained suppressed (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 4C.

claim: KCND3 levels remained suppressed despite Ad.KChIP2 treatment during phenylephrine stimulation.
source: Critically, maintaining KChIP2 levels through use of adenovirus encoding KChIP2 (Ad.KChIP2) normalized the expression of miRs-34b/c while reversing the loss in SCN5A and SCN1B; however, KCND3 levels remained suppressed (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from qPCR shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Phenylephrine treatment significantly reduced INa and Ito,f density in NRVMs.
source: Functional evaluation on both INa and Ito,f shows significant loss in density following PE treatment (Figure 4D and E), reflecting the changes we see in transcript expression and mimicking ion channel remodeling observed in HF.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Ad.KChIP2 treatment restored INa and Ito,f current density during phenylephrine treatment.
source: However, Ad.KChIP2 treatment restored the current density for both currents, despite KCND3 transcript expression being unaffected by KChIP2 expression.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Failing human heart tissue shows significant reduction of KChIP2 compared to non-failing tissue.
source: Moreover, we were able to observe significant reduction of KChIP2 and elevation of miR-34b/c within failing human heart tissue compared to non-failing (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from human tissue analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Failing human heart tissue shows elevation of miR-34b/c compared to non-failing tissue.
source: Moreover, we were able to observe significant reduction of KChIP2 and elevation of miR-34b/c within failing human heart tissue compared to non-failing (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from human tissue analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A predicted DRE motif exists proximal to the transcriptional start site in the human miR-34b/c promoter.
source: Reinforcing this conservation was the identification of a predicted DRE motif proximal to the transcriptional start site, in the human miR-34b/c promoter as evaluated by MatInspector (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computational analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Failing human heart tissue shows significant loss of SCN5A and KCND3 transcripts.
source: At the same time, significant loss of SCN5A and KCND3 transcripts in failing tissue (Figure 5C) also show conservation of miR-34b/c targeting within their 3'-UTRs (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from human tissue analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SCN1B does not preserve its miR-34b/c target site in humans.
source: Interestingly, SCN1B does not preserve its target site in humans, however, we also observed no significant reduction in transcript expression from failing heart tissue (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence analysis and qPCR shown in Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: miR-34b/c antimir treatment maintained INa in NRVMs during phenylephrine treatment.
source: Much like KChIP2 delivery which reduced miR-34b/c expression, directly blocking miR-34b/c activity maintained INa in both rat and iCells (Figure 6A and D), further implicating miR-34b/c in the direct regulation of these ion channel transcripts.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 6A.

claim: miR-34b/c antimir treatment maintained INa in human iCells during phenylephrine treatment.
source: Much like KChIP2 delivery which reduced miR-34b/c expression, directly blocking miR-34b/c activity maintained INa in both rat and iCells (Figure 6A and D), further implicating miR-34b/c in the direct regulation of these ion channel transcripts.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 6D.

claim: miR-34b/c block resulted in partial restoration of Ito,f in NRVMs during phenylephrine treatment.
source: In fact, by probing just Ito,f, we revealed a significant, but incomplete restoration following miR-34b/c block (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 6C.

claim: miR-34b/c block resulted in full restoration of Ito in human iCells during phenylephrine treatment.
source: Notably, the same experiment conducted in iCells where Kv4.3 is the dominant subunit, resulted in the full restoration of Ito (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 6E.

claim: miR-34b/c block did not rescue IKr in iCells during phenylephrine treatment.
source: To be more certain the restoration of current density was specific to miR-34b/c targeting the underlying subunits encoding INa and Ito, rather than a general rescue in the molecular state of the cell, the repolarizing current IKr was assessed in iCells. PE successfully reduced this current, which is known to be reduced by cardiac stressors, however, it was unable to be rescued by miR-34b/c block (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch clamp recordings shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Phenylephrine treatment for 48 hr caused sustained reentrant excitation in 5 of 7 NRVM monolayers with control antimirs.
source: Critically, this block was sufficient to cause sustained reentrant excitation in 5 of 7 monolayers (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: miR-34b/c inhibition prevented conduction block and protected all monolayers from sustained re-entry during phenylephrine treatment.
source: Remarkably, PE + miR-34b/c inhibition prevented conduction block and mitigated conduction slowing, protecting all monolayers from sustained re-entry (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Phenylephrine exposure for 48 hr significantly prolonged APD in NRVM monolayers.
source: Reflecting the changes in INa and Ito expression, exposure to PE for 48 hr significantly prolonged APD and slowed conduction velocity compared to control dishes across multiple pacing cycle lengths (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Phenylephrine exposure for 48 hr slowed conduction velocity in NRVM monolayers.
source: Reflecting the changes in INa and Ito expression, exposure to PE for 48 hr significantly prolonged APD and slowed conduction velocity compared to control dishes across multiple pacing cycle lengths (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7E.

claim: APD prolongation from phenylephrine was unresponsive to miR-34b/c inhibition in NRVMs.
source: APD prolongation from PE was unresponsive to miR-34b/c inhibition; however, this was anticipated as we previously determined Ito is not restored by miR-34b/c block in NRVM due to the additional Kv1.4 and Kv4.2 mediated current.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Phenylephrine treated cells displayed a significantly longer effective refractory period (ERP) than control cells.
source: Reflecting the prolonged APD and reduced INa, PE treated cells displayed a significantly longer ERP (Figure 7F) than control cells.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Treatment with miR-34 antimir significantly shortened ERP towards control during phenylephrine treatment.
source: However, treatment with the miR-34 antimir significantly shortened ERP towards control.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optical mapping shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Recovery of ERP by miR-34 antimir occurred in the absence of a shortened APD.
source: Notably, this recovery occurred in the absence of a shortened APD, suggesting a significant recovery of INa excitability.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data from Figure 7D and 7F.

claim: KChIP2 loss is a consistent event following cardiac stress.
source: Intriguingly, loss of the Potassium Channel Interacting Protein 2 (KChIP2) has proven to be a consistent event following cardiac stress, sparking interest into understanding its contribution in disease remodeling (Näbauer and Kääb, 1998; Nass et al., 2008; Jin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Aberrant remodeling in heart failure culminates in altered Ca2+ current (ICa).
source: Aberrant remodeling culminates in altered Ca2+ current (ICa) (Houser et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2008), Na+ current (INa) (Pu and Boyden, 1997; Maltsev et al., 2002), and a host of outward K+ currents (IK) (Näbauer and Kääb, 1998), creating impaired cardiac excitability and performance, accounting for high rates of mortality in HF patients (Nattel et al., 2007; Tomaselli and Zipes, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Aberrant remodeling in heart failure culminates in altered Na+ current (INa).
source: Aberrant remodeling culminates in altered Ca2+ current (ICa) (Houser et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2008), Na+ current (INa) (Pu and Boyden, 1997; Maltsev et al., 2002), and a host of outward K+ currents (IK) (Näbauer and Kääb, 1998), creating impaired cardiac excitability and performance, accounting for high rates of mortality in HF patients (Nattel et al., 2007; Tomaselli and Zipes, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Aberrant remodeling in heart failure culminates in altered outward K+ currents (IK).
source: Aberrant remodeling culminates in altered Ca2+ current (ICa) (Houser et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2008), Na+ current (INa) (Pu and Boyden, 1997; Maltsev et al., 2002), and a host of outward K+ currents (IK) (Näbauer and Kääb, 1998), creating impaired cardiac excitability and performance, accounting for high rates of mortality in HF patients (Nattel et al., 2007; Tomaselli and Zipes, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: KChIP3 (DREAM) is a transcriptional repressor that interacts with a nucleotide sequence known as the DRE motif.
source: This member of the KChIP family shares a high degree of homology with KChIP2, but more importantly has known transcriptional activity occurring through interaction with a nucleotide sequence known as the DRE motif (Carrión et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Transcriptional derepression of DREAM is regulated through Ca2+ binding to EF-hand motifs.
source: Additionally, it is known that transcriptional derepression of DREAM is regulated through Ca2+ binding to EF-hand motifs (Carrión et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Kv4.3 is the dominant contributor to Ito in the human background.
source: To further identify if the presence of Kv4.2, Kv4.3, and Kv1.4 in rats could explain the resisted change in Ito, cardiomyocytes derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iCells) were used, since in the human background, Kv4.3 is the dominant contributor to Ito (Niwa and Nerbonne, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Rapid depletion of KChIP2 protein is a widespread event that underlies remodeling in many cardiac diseases, including chronic HF, MI, and atrial fibrillation.
source: Rapid depletion of KChIP2 protein is a widespread event that underlies remodeling in many cardiac diseases, including chronic HF, MI, and atrial fibrillation (Nattel et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Cardiac diseases including chronic HF, MI, and atrial fibrillation present with reductions in Ito and INa.
source: Considerably, these diseases also present with reductions in Ito and INa.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge based on the context of the discussion.

claim: KChIP2 loss induces the destabilization of Kv4.2/4.3 channels and mediates the decline in current density.
source: The relationship between KChIP2 and Ito has been heavily studied, frequently identifying that KChIP2 loss induces the destabilization of Kv4.2/4.3 channels and mediates the decline in current density (Foeger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Reduced KChIP2 expression stimulated by phenylephrine + propranolol in NRVM cultures experienced increased Kv4.2 protein while KChIP2 and Kv4.3 levels were reduced.
source: However, it is also observed that reduced KChIP2 expression stimulated by phenylephrine + propranolol in in vitro cultures of NRVM experienced increased Kv4.2 protein while KChIP2 and Kv4.3 levels were reduced (Panama et al., 2011), supporting the opportunity for miRNA dependent translational block targeting Kv4.3, rather than just destabilization of all Kv4 channels.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: There is a loss in the full length transcript for Nav1.5 mRNA and a corresponding increase in a truncated isoform without the miR-34b/c target region in cardiac disease.
source: Notably, others have shown a loss in the full length transcript for Nav1.5 mRNA and a corresponding increase in a truncated isoform without the miR-34b/c target region present (Shang et al., 2007), reinforcing the observations for miR-34b/c mediating the decline of SCN5A.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Maintaining KChIP2 expression attenuated hypertrophy and pathogenic remodeling in a rat TAC banding model.
source: In a rat TAC banding model, it was observed that maintaining KChIP2 expression attenuated hypertrophy and pathogenic remodeling that otherwise lead to a worsening myocardium during pressure overload (Jin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The miR-34 family has been implicated in the development and progression of hypertrophy and heart failure in rodent models of both MI and pressure overload.
source: Indeed, the miR-34 family has recently been implicated in the development and progression of hypertrophy and heart failure, in rodent models of both MI and pressure overload (Bernardo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Blockade of the miR-34 family can attenuate pathologic remodeling in rodent models.
source: Critically, these studies, combined with our own data, show that blockade of the miR-34 family can attenuate pathologic remodeling, expanding the significance of KChIP2 and miR-34 in cardiac pathogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation and confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: KChIP2 null mice submitted to TAC banding show no worsened phenotype when compared to wild type mice.
source: Investigations conducted in KChIP2 null mice have shown that when submitted to TAC banding, there is no worsened phenotype when compared to wild type mice (Speerschneider et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Arrhythmia susceptibility was lowered in KChIP2 null mice during heart failure.
source: In fact, arrhythmia susceptibility was lowered in the KChIP2 null mice during heart failure, believed to be the result of reduced dispersion of repolarization.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Restoring KChIP2 expression in myocytes isolated from KChIP2 null mice resulted in no rescue of Kv4.2 protein expression or recovery of Ito,f.
source: Evidence for this is observed when restoring KChIP2 expression in myocytes isolated from KChIP2 null mice, which resulted in no rescue of Kv4.2 protein expression or recovery of Ito,f (Foeger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Restoration of KChIP2 following acute loss from pathologic consequences in a rat model was able to rescue Ito,f.
source: However, restoration of KChIP2 following acute loss from pathologic consequences in a rat model was able to rescue Ito,f (Jin et al., 2010), consistent with what we see in our own maintenance of KChIP2 following prolonged PE exposure (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation and confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: When INa becomes compromised, the vulnerability period increases.
source: As INa becomes compromised, it begins to resolve an expanding interval of premature stimuli declared the vulnerability period. Within this interval, reentry is more likely to occur as a result of non-uniform conduction block surrounding the point of excitation (Starmer et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: When Na+ channel availability is reduced, the vulnerable period increases.
source: Both theoretical (Starmer et al., 1991, 1993) and experimental (Nesterenko et al., 1992; Starmer et al., 1992) studies show that when Na+ channel availability is reduced, the vulnerable period increases.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Conduction block due to compromised cellular excitability has long been understood to be important for clinically relevant arrhythmias.
source: At the same time, conduction block due to compromised cellular excitability has long been understood to be important for clinically relevant arrhythmias (Shah et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Locked nucleic acids and related technologies have been used to successfully target miRNA activity in vivo.
source: Currently, the use of locked nucleic acids and related technologies have been used to successfully target miRNA activity in vivo (Olson, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: A gene expression array following 48 hr of KChIP2 silencing revealed an increase in expression for 293 genes and a decrease in expression for 407 genes.
source: Evaluation of genes that experienced at least a two fold change revealed an increase in expression for 293 genes and a decrease in expression for 407 genes in response to KChIP2 silencing (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from gene expression array analysis.

claim: Of the genes experiencing increased expression following KChIP2 silencing, 192 (65.5%) were predicted to contain a DRE motif within promoter elements.
source: Notably, of the genes experiencing increased expression, 192 of them (65.5%) were predicted to contain a DRE motif within promoter elements, implicating the potential of KChIP2 transcriptional activity directly mediating these changes.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computational analysis of gene expression array data.

claim: Of the genes responding with reduced expression following KChIP2 silencing, 71 (17.4%) were predicted to contain a miR-34b/c target site within their 3'-UTR.
source: Additionally, of the genes responding with reduced expression, 71 of them (17.4%) were predicted to contain a miR-34b/c target site within their 3'-UTR.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computational analysis of gene expression array data.

claim: KChIP2 regulates Cav1.2 through direct interaction with an inhibitory N-terminal domain on the channel.
source: Recent work has identified KChIP2 regulation of Cav1.2 through direct interaction with an inhibitory N-terminal domain on the channel, effectively reducing ICa,L in the absence of KChIP2 (Thomsen et al., 2009; Foeger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: KChIP2 is part of a larger macromolecular complex that includes subunits for both Nav1.5 and Kv4 channels.
source: Our previous work has also suggested that KChIP2 is part of a larger macromolecular complex that includes subunits for both Nav1.5 and Kv4 channels that lead to functional increases in both currents when coexpressed with KChIP2 (DeschenesDeschênes et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a prior finding with citation.

claim: KChIP3 interacts with and suppresses the activity of the cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB).
source: Even the role of KChIP3 as a transcriptional repressor is multimodal, including direct binding to DRE motifs, in addition to interacting with and suppressing the activity of the cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB), an established transcriptional activator (Ledo et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: KChIP3 has three functional high affinity EF-hand motifs.
source: Both of these processes are Ca2+ regulated, due to three functional high affinity EF-hand motifs residing in the protein (Carrión et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The entirety of the KChIP gene family displays strong conservation around EF-hand residues.
source: Given that the entirety of the KChIP gene family displays strong conservation around these EF-hand residues, suggests conservation of these Ca2+ regulated responses.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on sequence conservation.

claim: Kv4.2 does not contain a miR-34 target region in its 3'-UTR.
source: Given that Kv4.2 does not contain a miR-34 target region in its 3'-UTR, but still experiences degradation following KChIP2 loss, it is likely that both mechanisms contribute to the resulting loss in Ito,f.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on sequence analysis and experimental observations.

claim: Reduced KChIP2 expression stimulated by phenylephrine + propranolol in NRVM cultures experienced increased Kv4.2 protein.
source: However, it is also observed that reduced KChIP2 expression stimulated by phenylephrine + propranolol in in vitro cultures of NRVM experienced increased Kv4.2 protein while KChIP2 and Kv4.3 levels were reduced (Panama et al., 2011), supporting the opportunity for miRNA dependent translational block targeting Kv4.3, rather than just destabilization of all Kv4 channels.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: In rodent myocytes, Ito is comprised of the shared alpha subunits Kv4.2 and Kv4.3.
source: The current evaluation was conducted in rodent myocytes, where Ito is comprised of the shared alpha subunits Kv4.2 and Kv4.3, which comprise a fast component of Ito referred to as Ito,f.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Kv1.4 encodes a slow component of Ito, referred to as Ito,s.
source: Additionally, there are the contributions of Kv1.4, another potassium channel subunit, which encodes a slow component, referred to as Ito,s.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Ito,f and Ito,s are distinguished by their respective rates of recovery from inactivation.
source: These descriptions are attributed to the respective rates of recovery from inactivation for each of these channels (Niwa and Nerbonne, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Kv1.4 does not contain a miR-34 seed region.
source: Importantly, Kv4.2 and Kv1.4 do not contain a miR-34 seed region.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence analysis.

claim: 14 miRNAs decreased greater than two fold following KChIP2 silencing.
source: Notably, we also observed 14 miRNAs decreased greater than two fold (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from microarray data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A loss in miRNA expression is not consistent with the role of KChIP2 as a transcriptional repressor.
source: However, a loss in miRNA expression is not consistent with the role of KChIP2 as a transcriptional repressor, and also would not lead to a decrease in ion channel mRNA expression.
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference based on the proposed mechanism.
